notes: The pose editor is calmer and can add what the reader missed. The wall of eighteen joint chips is gone: tap a joint on the picture to select it, and one row names it with a Switch off button; only joints that are off are listed, to tap back on. A hand or foot the reader did not see now has an add button, which places a template at the wrist or ankle, sized and pointed on from the forearm or shin; every hand then has one handle at the middle fingertip and every foot one at the big toe, and dragging the handle turns and resizes the whole thing about its wrist or ankle while the wrist stays put. A flip button swaps the thumb or toe side for a hand seen from the other face. Mirror sits in the same row and covers hands and feet too. The lines over the picture are thinner and slightly see-through so the photo underneath stays readable while you work.
